title: Feedback-based quantum optimization with low depth and measurement
authors: Zi-Wen Huang, Jia-Cheng Fan, Xiao-Hui Ni, Su-Juan Qin, Xiao-Kai Hou, Wei Huang, Bing-Jie Xu, Fei Gao
abstract: Feedback-based ALgorithm for Quantum OptimizatioN (FALQON) is a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for solving combinatorial optimization problems, which circumvents classical parameter optimization but requires a deep quantum circuit. To reduce circuit depth, Arai et al. proposed second-order FALQON (SO-FALQON), achieving the best depth reduction among existing approaches. However, SO-FALQON brings a 2.3 times per-step measurement overhead, as it needs to calculate an additional second-order control coefficient. In this paper, inspired by the Backtracking Line Search (BLS) theory, we propose another method called BLS-FALQON, which not only reduces circuit depth to a comparable extent, but also achieves fewer measurements than SO-FALQON. Numerical simulations on max-cut problem with 8 to 20 vertices demonstrate that BLS-FALQON reduces the total measurement count by 37.7% compared to SO-FALQON, while maintaining a comparable circuit depth. Furthermore, we conduct real quantum hardware experiments on the Tianyan-176 quantum computer, which uses the zuchongzhi2 superconducting quantum processor, confirming that BLS-FALQON remains effective under real quantum hardware conditions.
summary: This paper introduces BLS-FALQON, an improved quantum optimization algorithm designed to solve combinatorial problems with minimal quantum resources. By integrating a backtracking line search into the feedback mechanism, it significantly reduces measurement overhead compared to existing state-of-the-art methods like SO-FALQON. The method is validated through both extensive simulations and real-world experiments on superconducting quantum hardware.
main_problem: Developing a quantum optimization algorithm that achieves low circuit depth and low measurement overhead for solving combinatorial optimization problems.
main_result: The proposed BLS-FALQON method reduces the total measurement count by 37.7% compared to SO-FALQON in simulations and reduces estimated hardware execution time by 43% on real quantum hardware.
method: The authors propose BLS-FALQON, which adapts the feedback-based quantum optimization framework by incorporating a backtracking line search mechanism inspired by BLS theory.
model_or_system: The work is based on the FALQON algorithm, which uses a time-dependent Hamiltonian $H(t) = H_p +  eta(t)H_d$ to drive the expectation value of the problem Hamiltonian $\langle H_p angle$ to decrease monotonically. Simulations use the max-cut problem, and experiments are performed on the Tianyan-176 quantum computer.
key_observables: The primary observables are the expectation values $\langle H_p angle$, and the key metrics are circuit depth and total measurement count.
important_parameters: The time step $\Delta t$, the control coefficient $ eta(t)$, and the backtracking factor $	au \in (-1, 0)$ are important parameters.
main_assumptions: The core assumption for BLS-FALQON is that the backtracking mechanism guarantees a valid descent step ($\Delta E < 0$) by iteratively adjusting the control coefficient $ eta^{(FO)}$ until the expectation value decreases.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes, but the results compare the performance (measurement count, depth, time) of BLS-FALQON against SO-FALQON and FALQON across simulations and hardware tests.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the FALQON framework, compares it to SO-FALQON, and then proposes and analyzes BLS-FALQON using theoretical proofs (Proposition 1) and validating it with numerical simulations and real quantum hardware experiments.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses resource limitations (depth and measurement overhead) in variational quantum algorithms, which is crucial for scaling quantum computation to practical problems.
